messages.subject: rank(v,s) in Nimble code
parts:
Hi NIMBLE experts!
I am creating a Netwrok Meta Analysis in NIMBLE. However, when computing the rank probabilities, I need to use the rank(b[], s) function in the code. It is available in other BUGS languages, as in WinBUGS, but for any reason, it is not here.
I found an alternative to implement the rank() function, using NimbleRCall. However, it is too slow. I found NimbleExternalCall would be much faster, but I do not have knowledge of C. Could you help in implementing this C call? Thanks

messages.author: 8a8dac569c928102
messages.subject: Re: rank(v,s) in Nimble code
parts:
Here is the first attempt, but it gives some errors. Also, it does not have the possiibility to extract the index directly in the function, only returns the rank vector.


sink('rank.h')
cat('
 extern "C" {
 void rank_function(double *p, double*ans, int n);
 }
')
sink()
sink('rank.cpp')
cat('
#include <cstdio>
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include "rank.h"

struct MyStruct {
    double value;
    int index;
    bool operator<(const MyStruct &other) const {
        return value < other.value;
    }
};

void rank_function(double *p, double *ans, int n) {
    MyStruct *s = new MyStruct[n];
    for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        s[i].value = p[i];
        s[i].index = i;
    }
    std::sort(s, s+n);
    int current_rank = 1;
    for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if(i>0 && s[i-1].value!=s[i].value) current_rank = i + 1;
        ans[s[i].index] = current_rank;
    }
    delete s;
}

')
sink()
system('g++ rank.cpp -c -o rank.o')
Rrank <- nimbleExternalCall(function(x = double(1), ans = double(1),
                                     n = integer()){}, Cfun =  'rank_function',
                            headerFile = file.path(getwd(), 'rank.h'), returnType = void(),
                            oFile = file.path(getwd(), 'rank.o'))
model_rank <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1)) {
    ans <- numeric(length(x))
    Rrank(x, ans, length(x))
    return(ans)
    returnType(double(1))
  })

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: rank(v,s) in Nimble code
parts:
Hi Javier,

Thanks for posting the question and taking a try at solving it.  I really don't remember why we didn't end up with rank and associated functions supported!  That might be something we should circle back on.  But also I think you can get what you need like this:

library(nimble)

m <- nimbleModel(
  nimbleCode({
    r <- sum(b[1:n] <= b[s]) # This is what rank(b, s) in BUGS does, I think
  }),
  constants = list(n = 10)
)

# Test it uncompiled:
set.seed(100)
m$b <- rnorm(10)
m$s <- 3
m$calculate('r')
m$r   # Here is the answer calculated in the model
rank(m$b)[m$s]  # Here is the answer calculated directly in R.  They match.

# Test it compiled
cm <- compileNimble(m)
cm$calculate('r')
cm$r  # Here is the answer calculated in the compiled model.
 
If you want to try writing versions yourself, usually the easiest place to start is with a nimbleFunction.  E.g.

myrank <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), i = double()) {
    ans <- 0
    val <- x[i]
    for(j in 1:length(x))
      ans <- ans + (x[j] <= val)
    return(ans)
    returnType(double())
  }
)

m <- nimbleModel(
  nimbleCode({
    r <- myrank(b[1:n], s)
  }),
  constants = list(n = 10)
)

set.seed(100)
m$b <- rnorm(10)
m$s <- 3
m$calculate('r')
m$r
rank(m$b)[m$s]

cm <- compileNimble(m)
cm$calculate('r')
cm$r

The nimbleFunction will be generated to C++ and compiled, so it should be fast.

HTH!
Perry
